answer: Each agent runs inside a TEE that emits a signed attestation containing a unique hardware UUID and a one‑time nonce whispered to a ledger’s river of proofs; the ledger stores the UUID in a timber‑hashed Merkle tree and rejects any duplicate entry. When a new agent registers, the ledger checks the tree; if the UUID already exists the registration fails. An attacker must purchase distinct TEEs, each costing $2,500 and lock a 24‑hour bonding period per identity, so forging N agents costs N × $2,500 plus 24 hours per fake.
